assessment.reason: F-MR06 composes SNOW into the existing F-MR05/F-KT kernel path; no alternate SWAP kernel is introduced.
SNOW composition uses structured parameters/state/forcing and runtime adapters; no file parsing, paths or file units are added to the kernel.
snow parameters, persistent snow state, snow forcing, numerical transaction configuration and results/diagnostics remain distinct data categories.
only snow-active columns allocate persistent snow continuation state; snow-inactive identity and zero snow-state allocation are tested.
no Newton/Jacobian/constitutive scratch is added per column; solver workspace ownership remains the existing serialized worker/job path.

F-MR06 reuses the already-computed canonical execution-order vector for deterministic aggregate accounting and adds no second sort. The pre-existing F-MR core insertion-sort execution-order implementation remains a separate scalability/performance concern and is not claimed qualified for 100k columns by F-MR06.
SNOW state participates in the existing F-KT checkpoint/candidate/rollback/replay/commit path; rejected trials do not publish committed snow state and rollback/replay/commit tests pass.
replay from the same committed state is bitwise stable and A/B/A repeatability passes; no warm-start shortcut changes physical origin state.

runtime interval remains explicit [t0,t1]. The exact-one-day duration restriction is an explicit scientific SNOW admission constraint inherited from F-VQ16, not a hidden kernel day/calendar assumption; non-midnight one-day is allowed and subdaily/multiday fail closed.
no coupling-window restriction is added; groundwater coupling remains outside this F-MR06 composition.
existing F-KT transaction semantics remain coupling-compatible; no new coupling physics or rollback semantics are introduced.
groundwater head/flux interface contract is untouched.

authoritative accepted mass remains F-KT-owned, complete with missing-contribution mask zero; snow storage and external snow/rain/sublimation terms are included and melt is counted once as an internal transfer. No new or relaxed mass tolerance is added.
interface-sensitivity outputs are untouched.
F-MR06 adds no coupling predictor/corrector run multiplication.

1/2/17/31 real-physics MultiSWAP cases pass with one reusable serialized physical worker and deterministic per-column identity. F-MR06 does not claim production-scale 100k-column throughput qualification.
tile fractions and MODFLOW-cell aggregation remain outside SWAP kernel/runtime physics composition.
deep-vadose transfer remains an external optional component.
no deep-vadose/direct-coupling transition is introduced.
F-MR06 reuses the existing soil-water/backend interfaces and does not couple other modules to HeadCalc internals.
the exact F-VQ16-admitted SNOW process blob is reused without formula changes and existing restricted Richards physics remains unchanged.
MultiSWAP runtime does not call HeadCalc directly; source-bound gates enforce the established backend boundary.
snow_active is explicit physical configuration while serialized execution remains an execution constraint; no reference/balanced/throughput/fallback policy or Richards physics is silently changed.
no bounded-cost or fallback production policy is introduced; solver-cost policy remains outside F-MR06.
snow-inactive F-MR05/F-MR04 reference route, mass and committed-state identity remain exact; full reference mechanisms are not removed.

per-column transaction/solver/mass provenance and batch requested/admitted/executed/committed/rejected, physical solve count, maximum simultaneous solves, deterministic collection and aggregate mass diagnostics remain available.
snow persistent state exists only for snow-active columns; inactive allocation/processing behavior is explicitly tested.
SNOW/runtime composition remains outside the kernel and contains no MODFLOW cell/tile ownership knowledge.
the one-day SNOW restriction is explicit and fail-closed as a process-specific admitted time domain; no midnight, file-format or direct-MODFLOW dependency is hidden in the runtime.

F-MR06 dependencies, ownership, source blobs, transaction/event semantics, mass accounting, optional-state behavior, failure history, deterministic-order correction, O0/O2 tests and scope holds are machine-readably recorded.

hard_holds: F-MR06 engineering tests do not independently scientifically admit the composed source; F-VQ requalification remains mandatory.
F-MQ24 must not release SNOW MultiSWAP before the composed F-MR06 candidate passes independent F-VQ.
Exact F-VQ16 one-call-daily SNOW scope remains the only SNOW scientific scope; subdaily and arbitrary-duration SNOW remain NOT_ADMITTED.
Richards remains the existing restricted equilibrium scientific slice used by the F-MR05/F-VQ15 lineage; no general non-equilibrium Richards expansion is implied.
Parallel real-physics execution remains NOT_ADMITTED; measured max simultaneous real physical solves is one.
No performance/fallback/relaxed numerical policy is admitted by F-MR06.
Pre-existing F-MR core execution-order sorting scalability is not solved or production-scale qualified by F-MR06.
